findings.title: Regular-payment command disagrees with Draft eligibility
findings.expected: A canonical command should enforce or explicitly distinguish the eligibility result exposed to its callers.
findings.observed: Both synthetic Customer Draft Quotes report paymentAllowed:false and the ordinary UI blocks regular payments, but ProgramQuotes.recordPayment accepts a Bank transfer. Deposits and reversal lineage/idempotency pass.
findings.impact: An alternate caller can create a transaction the normal UI considers unavailable. A user-interface bypass and an approved prohibition on all pre-Issue receipts were not established; this is not a Critical-gate failure.
findings.action: Confirm the intended pre-Issue payment policy, then align canonical and UI eligibility in a bounded change.

findings.title: Approved UI changes have left release tests stale
findings.expected: Tests should match the no-Paste MetroMap modal and three-level inspector disclosure.
findings.observed: Inspected MetroMap cases request the removed Paste button. Two executed deep Undo cases assume the second collapse click reopens full; it correctly reaches minimal, where vertex controls are hidden. An independent current-behavior procedure passes for both modes.
findings.impact: The unmodified browser/release aggregate cannot provide reliable current sign-off. These failures do not demonstrate broken Undo or MetroMap activation.
findings.action: Update obsolete assertions under separate authorisation and separate desktop functional cases from excluded screenshot/mobile checks.

findings.title: Latest converted workspace retains 57 Data Health warnings
findings.expected: Structural recovery and business readiness must be assessed separately.
findings.observed: The latest approved fixture has zero validation errors, duplicate IDs, missing links or foreign records. It retains 57 warnings for status migration readiness, missing operational amount and an active legacy catalogue.
findings.impact: The backup is structurally recoverable, but its status/funding/catalogue choices need operational review before relying on them. No source data was silently corrected.
findings.action: Review warnings in a disposable imported copy, record accepted exceptions or corrections, and preserve the approved original.

findings.title: Superseded automatic-Job wording remains in gate documents
findings.expected: Cross-references should reflect the accepted 1 October explicit-calendar decision.
findings.observed: DECISIONS explicitly supersedes automatic Operational Task Job creation, while older Constitution/PC-027/Gate Q clauses still describe it. The readiness test README also calls a now-included fixture private/unbundled.
findings.impact: Future reviewers may report false noncompliance or reinstate deliberately removed behavior. This audit follows the later accepted ADR and owner changes.
findings.action: Reconcile current cross-references and fixture wording in a documentation-only change; retain historical records.

findings.title: Lockfile advisory checks exclude the old vendored PDF runtime
findings.expected: Security evidence should include browser libraries shipped outside package-lock.
findings.observed: The npm query reports zero known vulnerabilities for its 34-dependency lockfile graph. Vendored PDF.js is 2.16.105, MapLibre is 5.3.0 and JSZip is 3.10.1. PDF.js falls in the CVE-2024-4367 range, but the importer sets isEvalSupported:false, the maintainer-documented mitigation. The separate reviewed 2026 advisory targets a newer version range.
findings.impact: A zero npm count alone would overstate shipped-runtime coverage. No malicious-PDF exploit or active credential exposure was demonstrated.
findings.action: Inventory vendored versions in repeatable advisory checks and assess a compatible supported PDF upgrade; preserve the explicit eval mitigation.

findings.title: CSS override density increases maintenance cost
findings.expected: Use existing shared tokens and remove only declarations proven redundant in their actual cascade.
findings.observed: styles.css has 11065 lines, 388715 bytes, 1891 !important declarations, 1236 hex-colour literals and 686 shared-token references. Approximately 160 selector groups repeat; media contexts are not normalised.
findings.impact: These source metrics do not prove unused CSS, a rendering slowdown or a visual defect.
findings.action: Consolidate one module at a time and verify computed styles before deleting overrides. No wholesale redesign is warranted.

findings.type: Auditability observation; no explicit mandatory actor rule found
findings.title: Reversal evidence does not identify the reversing officer
findings.expected: Exact commercial lineage, reason, time and idempotency are required; named officer attribution would improve evidence.
findings.observed: Synthetic reversals preserve reason, timestamp, Quote/Project/owner and original records. reversedBy is not written even with a synthetic session operator name; the viewer truthfully displays Not recorded.
findings.impact: Commercial traceability passes, while person-level attribution is absent. PC-009 does not explicitly require a named reversal actor; no authenticated-identity rule is invented.
findings.action: Decide whether explicit reversal-officer attribution should become a product requirement.
